lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Remember those falling-sand games where you pour pixels and watch them pile up? Here's one running on a Nintendo Switch.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's nxsand. It's a falling-sand simulation for the Switch, with a desktop target so it's easy to develop.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How does the sand actually work?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Every material lives in a grid of integers. Simulation passes update that grid, step by step, like a cellular automaton.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A separate rendering path turns those material identifiers into the image you see, using the GPU. It's mostly C plus plus.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So simulation and drawing are kept apart.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, and that's what keeps it fast. The full write-up has more.
